name: ZAMBIA

flag.title: Flag of Zambia
flag.note: Green with orange eagle, red & black stripes

lead: Zambia sits in the heart of Africa, far from any sea. The Zambezi River drops 108 m over Victoria Falls. Zambia won freedom from Britain in 1964 and took its name from the river. It has 20 national parks.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Zambia sits on a high, flat land that averages 1,200 m. Three great rivers cross it: the Zambezi, the Kafue and the Luangwa. Lake Tanganyika, one of the world's deepest lakes, touches the north.
Victoria Falls is called Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'. In flood season, spray rises 400 m.
animals: In South Luangwa Park, you can track lions and leopards on foot. Kafue National Park is as big as Switzerland. Wild dogs, cheetahs and buffalo herds live there.
Hippos and crocodiles fill the Zambezi. The shoebill is a huge grey bird that stands still for hours. Thornicroft's giraffe lives nowhere else on Earth.
culture: Zambia has 70+ groups of people, but its motto is 'One Zambia, One Nation'. Each February, the Ngoni people perform Nc'wala to give thanks for the harvest.
Nshima is a thick corn porridge. People roll it into a ball and dip it in fish or beans. Chitenge, a boldly patterned cloth, makes skirts and headscarves.
history: The Lozi kingdom ruled the flooded plains of Barotse, and the Bemba held the north. The explorer David Livingstone reached Victoria Falls in 1855. By 1924, Britain ruled Northern Rhodesia.
Zambia became independent on 24 October 1964, with Kenneth Kaunda as first president. Copper brought wealth, but prices fell in the 1970s. Growth has been steady since the 1990s.
wows: Victoria Falls, 1,708 m wide, is the world's largest waterfall by width and height combined.
The Zambia–Zimbabwe border runs through the middle of Victoria Falls.
Kafue National Park covers 22,400 km², larger than Wales.
Zambia was among Africa's first TV broadcasters, in 1961.
The shoebill stands over 1.5 m tall, with a beak like a wooden shoe.
Rapids below the falls are Class 5, the hardest people can raft.
Zambia holds over 40% of Africa's fresh lake and river water.

myths.myth: Zambia and Zimbabwe are one country
myths.fact: No. They are neighbours, split by the Zambezi. Zambia was Northern Rhodesia, Zimbabwe Southern Rhodesia.

myths.myth: Hippos are too fat to run
myths.fact: On land, a hippo can sprint faster than a person, up to about 30 km/h.
